description: Nuxt project states and rule cases whose @nuxt/eslint behaviour @vizejs/nuxt-lint-config, the Nuxt runtime emitter, and Vize Patina must reproduce. Project cases are materialised under a scratch root by oracle.mjs; every path is expressed relative to that root so the recording stays machine-independent.

checkerCases.description: An empty checker object takes every portable upstream default.
checker: true is identical to an empty checker object.
Every portable checker option passes through without being widened or dropped.

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Every direct Vue context API pinned by upstream is rejected at definePageMeta's eager level.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ values: [ref(), shallowRef(), customRef(), computed(), reactive(), shallowReactive(), readonly(), shallowReadonly(), toRef(), toRefs(), watch(), watchEffect(), watchPostEffect(), watchSyncEffect(), effectScope(), onScopeDispose(), onBeforeMount(), onMounted(), onBeforeUpdate(), onUpdated(), onBeforeUnmount(), onUnmounted(), onActivated(), onDeactivated(), onErrorCaptured(), onRenderTracked(), onRenderTriggered(), onServerPrefetch(), inject(), getCurrentInstance()] })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Only direct identifiers matching /^use[A-Z]/ are treated as composables beyond the fixed context API list.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ values: [useRoute(), useFetch(), useA(), useURL(), usefoo(), use_Foo(), UseFoo(), abuseFoo(), use1(), useÅ()] })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Eager this and the complete await expression are rejected; a context call under await also keeps its own diagnostic.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ owner: this, title: await fetchTitle(), route: await useRoute() })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Arrow, function-expression, and object-method bodies form lazy boundaries where context values, this, and await are valid.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ middleware: () => useRoute(), validate: async function () { await ref(); return this }, method() { return computed() } })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Member, sequence, and new-expression callees stay valid; optional direct calls and direct calls nested in other arguments are rejected.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ a: Vue.ref(), b: nuxt.useRoute(), c: (0, useRoute)(), d: new useRoute(), e: useRoute?.(), f: wrapper(useFetch()) })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: The upstream rule is syntax-only, so parameters shadowing a context API or composable remain diagnostics.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: function page(ref, useRoute) { return definePageMeta({ a: ref(), b: useRoute() }) }

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Only direct definePageMeta calls create a boundary, each sequential macro is visited, and values outside or under member callees stay valid.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: const outside = ref(); definePageMeta({ a: ref() }); definePageMeta({ b: useRoute() }); Nuxt.definePageMeta({ c: computed() }); _definePageMeta({ d: useFetch() })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Computed keys, arrays, object spreads, this, and nested macro arguments remain at the enclosing eager level.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ [useRoute()]: { nested: [computed(), { value: this }] }, spread: { ...useState() }, inner: definePageMeta({ value: watchEffect() }) })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: Function boundaries cover default parameters as well as bodies, while an adjacent eager value is still rejected.
noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.source: definePageMeta({ middleware: (value = useRoute()) => computed(value), validate: function (value = ref()) { return this }, outside: shallowRef() })

noPageMetaRuntimeValuesCases.description: An optional direct definePageMeta call still forms the macro boundary, while empty and identifier-only arguments stay valid.

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: Both boolean values are rejected when direct identifier test keys occur in the default-exported object.
The first object argument of any default-exported call is inspected, independent of the callee name; later arguments are ignored.
noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.source: export default customWrapper({ test: false }, { test: true })

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: A member-expression callee also qualifies because upstream constrains only the first argument shape.
A computed identifier key still matches because upstream checks its Identifier node and name without checking the computed flag.
Quoted, computed-literal, differently cased, and longer property keys remain valid.
noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.source: export default { 'test': true, ['test']: false, testing: true, Test: false }

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: Only boolean literal values match; identifiers, numbers, strings, null, calls, shorthands, and methods remain valid.
noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.source: const test = true; const enabled = true; export default { test, test: enabled, test: 1, test: 'true', test: null, test: Boolean(true), test() { return true } }

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: An object behind an identifier and a non-exported wrapper call are not traversed as Nuxt config exports.
noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.source: const config = { test: true }; defineNuxtConfig({ test: false }); export default config

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: Only direct properties of the first exported object argument are inspected; nested and later objects remain valid.
noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.source: export default defineNuxtConfig({ nested: { test: true }, values: [{ test: false }] }, { test: true })

noNuxtConfigTestKeyCases.description: Parentheses do not change the default-exported object shape seen by the upstream parser.
Parentheses around the exported call and its first object argument are transparent in the upstream ESTree shape.
Parentheses around a computed identifier key and boolean value remain transparent to the upstream parser.
An escaped identifier spelling still has the semantic Identifier name test and must not be lost by the byte prefilter.
The diagnostic spans the complete property, including comments between its key, colon, and boolean value.

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: The complete pinned key table, all official modules, and three environment keys sort into the exact upstream order.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { hooks: null, logLevel: null, debug: null, telemetry: null, test: null, postcss: null, typescript: null, webpack: null, vite: null, devServerHandlers: null, serverHandlers: null, hub: null, nitro: null, compatibilityDate: null, experimental: null, features: null, future: null, watchers: null, watch: null, devServer: null, dev: null, optimization: null, sourcemap: null, routeRules: null, generate: null, build: null, builder: null, ignorePrefix: null, ignoreOptions: null, ignore: null, extensions: null, alias: null, analyzeDir: null, modulesDir: null, buildDir: null, serverDir: null, workspaceDir: null, appDir: null, srcDir: null, rootDir: null, dir: null, runtimeConfig: null, appConfig: null, spaLoadingTemplate: null, ui: null, mdc: null, content: null, colorMode: null, site: null, unhead: null, router: null, vue: null, css: null, app: null, devtools: null, imports: null, components: null, pages: null, ssr: null, $test: true, $production: true, $development: true, plugins: null, modules: null, theme: null, extends: null, buildId: null, appId: null }

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: An ordered direct object stays byte-identical and produces no diagnostic or fix.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default defineNuxtConfig({ modules: [], $development: {}, ssr: true, app: {}, vite: {}, hooks: {} })

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Multiline comments, indentation, and upstream's inserted trailing comma are preserved exactly.
Top-level and identifier-keyed environment objects report together and converge across repeated fix passes.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { ssr: true, $test: { ssr: true, modules: [] }, $production: { build: {}, app: {} }, modules: [] }

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Known keys lead, while unknown identifier and raw literal keys use upstream locale collation.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { zebra: 1, "ssr": true, modules: [], 'app': {}, css: [], alpha: 2 }

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Computed identifiers, methods, and shorthands use their identifier names; computed literals retain raw-key ordering.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { [ssr]: true, modules, ["app"]: {}, css, app() {} }

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Spreads remain fixed and independently bound the sortable property segments around them.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { modules: [], ssr: true, ...base, css: [], app: {}, ...tail, vite: {}, build: {} }

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: A parenthesized object in the first argument of any default-exported call is inspected.
Identifier-backed exports, non-exported calls, and objects in later call arguments are not traversed.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: const config = { ssr: true, modules: [] }; const local = wrap({ ssr: true, modules: [] }); export default wrap(extra, { ssr: true, modules: [] })

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Empty and single-property exported objects need no sorting and remain byte-identical.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: const empty = {}; export default defineNuxtConfig({ ssr: true })

nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.description: Unknown ASCII keys use localeCompare's lowercase-first, case-insensitive primary ordering.
nuxtConfigKeysOrderCases.source: export default { zebra: 1, Zebra: 2, alpha: 3, Alpha: 4 }

importGlobals.description: Nuxt and Nitro auto-import registries are merged, sorted by source then imported name, and aliases become readonly globals.

preferImportMetaCases.description: Every suffix accepted by @nuxt/eslint-plugin is diagnosed and preserves its name in the replacement.
preferImportMetaCases.source: const flags = [process.client, process.browser, process.server, process.nitro, process.dev, process.test, process.prerender]

preferImportMetaCases.description: A computed identifier property matches because upstream checks the property node type and name, not the computed flag.
Optional member access is reported and the whole optional expression is replaced.
Only the inner process member is replaced when another member is chained after it.
Upstream intentionally remains syntax-only and reports a lexically shadowed process parameter.
A matching member used as an assignment target is still reported and fixed.
String keys, unknown identifiers, and process below another receiver do not satisfy the upstream AST predicate.
preferImportMetaCases.source: const values = [process['client'], process[mode], state.process.client, process.production, import.meta.client]

preferImportMetaCases.description: Comments, strings, differently cased identifiers, and object keys are not member expressions rooted at process.
preferImportMetaCases.source: const text = 'process.server'; /* process.dev */ const values = [PROCESS.client, myprocess.server, { process: { client: true } }]

preferImportMetaCases.description: Multiple findings keep exact non-overlapping ranges and are fixed together.

dirDefaultCases.description: A hand-written config with no dirs at all takes every default.
Declaring src derives every per-feature directory from it.
Declaring root makes src follow root rather than the built-in pair.
Present-but-empty lists are kept: an empty array is truthy, so the ||= defaults never fire.
Only the missing lists are defaulted; declared ones pass through untouched.

cases.description: Nuxt 4 defaults: a single layer with srcDir app/.
Nuxt 3 layout where srcDir equals rootDir, so every directory is top level.
A base layer extended by the app layer; every directory list gains a second entry.
nuxt.options.dir renames pages, layouts, plugins, middleware and modules.
Extra auto-import directories, including a tilde-prefixed entry.
components declared as a bare array of directory strings.
components declared as objects, one of which carries a prefix.
components: true keeps the default components directory.
No feature options: standalone on, stylistic off, config-key sorting off.
standalone: false drops the baseline blocks, keeping only the Nuxt-aware ones.
stylistic: true also switches nuxt.config key sorting on.
An explicit sortConfigKeys: false overrides the stylistic default.
sortConfigKeys can be enabled without stylistic rules.
typescript: false drops the TypeScript blocks from the baseline.
typescript: true adds the TypeScript blocks regardless of package detection.
tooling: true adds the module-author rule blocks.
